subject: Data Engineering
title: Normalization vs Denormalization
description: A micro-lesson that makes Normalization vs Denormalization usable.

hook.text: Database textbooks say: normalize everything. Warehouse practitioners say: denormalize aggressively.

buildup.text: Normalization eliminates redundancy. Every fact is stored exactly once, saving space and consistency.

discovery.text: Denormalization copies data into fewer, wider tables — trading redundancy for faster read performance.

twist.text: In transactional systems, normalization prevents update anomalies. In warehouses, reads dominate.

climax.text: The right level of normalization depends on whether the workload is write-heavy or read-heavy.

punchline.text: Normalize for writes. Denormalize for reads.

quiz.question: Why do data warehouses favor denormalization?
options: Fewer joins make analytical queries faster
